newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says conditions not ripe for NATO return.
newsitem.headline: France says conditions not ripe for NATO return.

text.p: France said on Wednesday conditions were not yet ripe for it to return to full membership of NATO's military wing and insisted the alliance should take in five new members, not just the three accepted by the United States.

In a statement issued after conservative President Jacques Chirac discussed the issue with Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, the Foreign Ministry said France wanted "to continue discussions with its allies to seek a better balance of responsibilities between Europeans and Americans."

The statement made clear that Chirac, who initiated France's rapprochement with the Atlantic Alliance in 1995, shared the new left-wing government's assessment that the United States had not yielded sufficient power to the European allies to justify a French return. Paris had demanded in vain that Washington hand over NATO's key southern command, which controls the Mediterranean, to a European.

"In the current state of negotiations, while noting that progress has been achieved, notably in affirming a European defence identity, France considers that the conditions it posed for re-examining its relations with NATO's military structures are not met," it said.
Chirac's office reacted with irritation last Friday when the Socialist-run Foreign Ministry made known its view without waiting for the president's formal decision.

"Concerning enlargement, France reaffirms that five countries now meet the conditions for joining the Alliance," the ministry said, alluding to Romania and Slovenia, as well as the three Washington accepts: the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.
